# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Banner Health — Member Appeals
*(Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if you are reading a copy, the filing address can be confirmed by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.)*

**From:** Riley Foster
Member ID: W204716433
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-22**
**Reference number:** POC-D5606CAED3-36942
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Plan:** Banner Health (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Governing policy:** *eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures* — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-22 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am respectfully asking Banner Health to reconsider that decision, because my medical records document exactly the kind of imaging, symptoms, function loss and failed conservative care that the plan's own shoulder surgery policy looks for.

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

## What the plan's own policy says, and what my records show

The policy identified above sets out, in the plan's own words, the building blocks it uses to decide whether shoulder surgery is medically necessary. Two of those passages read:

> " MRI or CT shows labral tear/biceps tendon pa thology (e.g., S LAP, full-thickness subscapularis tear) and correlates with the individual’s reported symptoms and physical exam findings  P hysical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings (as compared to the non-involved side):"

> " O’ Brien’s test  Biceps load test  Clunk test  Anterior slide test  Compression rotation test  Speed’s test  Modified dynamic labral shear  Function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)  Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration  Other potential pathological cond itions have been excluded including, but not limited to, the following:"

I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about one thing: the passages I have quoted above are the plan's verbatim language from the sections of this policy addressing labral repair and biceps tenodesis. I have not been given, and therefore have not quoted, the section of this policy that lists the criteria specific to rotator cuff repair. I am not going to put words in the plan's mouth. What the quoted language does show is the framework this policy applies to shoulder surgery — advanced imaging that correlates with the symptoms and the physical exam, function-limiting pain, and failure of at least three months of provider-directed non-surgical care. My records address each of those elements directly.

**1. Imaging, and how it correlates with my symptoms and exam.** This is the specific basis given for the denial, so I want to set the record out plainly. My MRI of the shoulder on 2026-07-06 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. My reported symptoms are 18 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. A full-thickness tear on MRI, positive provocative testing on that same shoulder, and 18 months of pain in that same shoulder are consistent findings pointing to one problem in one joint. I would ask the reviewer to confirm that the MRI report of 2026-07-06, the physical therapy discharge note, and Dr. Okafor's operative request were all in front of the person who made this determination.

**2. Function-limiting pain.** The policy language quoted above describes function-limiting pain as loss of shoulder function that interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living. My records state that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. Those are basic daily activities, and I have lost them.

**3. Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months.** My records document supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics — 24 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, with a discharge note; NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21 that gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, that is more than three months of provider-directed conservative care, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**4. Other considerations.** My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Banner Health to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-22 and authorize the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by Dr. Okafor. Specifically, I ask that:

1. My complete file be re-reviewed against the *eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures* policy, including the MRI report of 2026-07-06, the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, and my surgeon's clinical documentation;
2. The review be conducted by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery; and
3. If the denial is upheld, I be told in writing which specific criterion of that policy my records do not meet, and what documentation would satisfy it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-18, which is 180 days from the date of the notice, and I am submitting it within that window. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; anyone reviewing this can also confirm the correct filing location by calling the number on the back of my insurance card and asking where member appeals are filed.

Please contact me at [my phone number] or [my email address] if anything further is needed. I would rather supply a missing document than have this decided on an incomplete file.

Thank you for taking another look.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
Riley Foster
Member ID: W204716433
Reference number: POC-D5606CAED3-36942
[My mailing address]
[My phone number] | [My email address]
Date: [Date signed]

**Enclosures (please check the ones you include):**
- [ ] Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-22
- [ ] MRI report, shoulder, 2026-07-06
- [ ] Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, 24 visits)
- [ ] Office notes from Dr. Okafor, MD
- [ ] Medication and injection records (NSAIDs; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-21)
- [ ] [Any other records you wish to attach]
